sections.heading: Vienna rectifier modulation
sections.text: The Vienna rectifier is a unidirectional three-phase PWM boost rectifier with inherent three-level modulation. Current control is typically in dq frame. Neutral-point voltage balancing is an additional control requirement that adjusts the common-mode duty-cycle offset.

sections.heading: Vienna vs conventional bridge
sections.text: Vienna rectifier advantages: only three active switches (vs six in conventional bridge), inherent three-level modulation reduces input current THD, no shoot-through risk. Limitation: unidirectional power flow only (boost mode). Neutral-point balancing required for three-level operation.
